elements.element: Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence
elements.evidence: "commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence"
"professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000"

elements.element: Cyber/privacy USD 5M where vendor processes Customer Data
elements.evidence: "where Commerce One processes Corio or Customer data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000"

elements.evidence: "workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law"
"certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request"

elements.element: Obligation imposed on Vendor (Commerce One), at its expense, for the term
elements.evidence: "Commerce One shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement"
"errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000" (exceeds 1M)
"cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000" (exceeds 2M)

reasons: All preferred atomic elements are expressly present: CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M conditioned on processing of Corio/Customer data, statutory workers' compensation, and certificates upon request, all imposed on the Vendor at its own expense.
Party direction is correct: the duty runs from Commerce One (Vendor) to Corio (Customer/Licensee).

Minimality fails on the official gate: a missing clause should be added by insert_after only, but operation 2 is a replace that renumbers the untouched Complete Understanding section ("14.11 Complete Understanding.").
The inserted "and for one (1) year thereafter" post-termination coverage tail is not required by the preferred position and is extra language beyond what is needed to complete the level.
Intent is preserved: the bankruptcy and entire-agreement provisions remain fully effective, no undefined terms are introduced, and the added clause creates no contradiction or dangling mechanic.
